newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan subway cult's hearthrob jailed for perjury.
newsitem.headline: Japan subway cult's hearthrob jailed for perjury.

text.p: The spokesman for the doomsday cult accused of the Tokyo subway gas attack received a three-year prison term on Monday for perjury and forgery.

Fumihiro Joyu, 34, was the public face of Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) after the sarin nerve gas attack two years ago on the Tokyo subway system. Handsome and articulate, he won admirers among teenage girls in his many media appearances as the cult's "information minister".
Chief Judge Hironobu Takezaki at Tokyo District Court said Joyu conspired with other cult members to give false testimony and forge documents in connection with a land purchase.
"He played a central part in plotting and carrying out the crimes. In court he has continued to avoid facing reality," the judge said in passing sentence.
But Takezaki said Joyu's guilt was partly mitigated by the fact that he had been acting on the instructions of cult guru Shoko Asahara.
Asahara is on trial for murder for masterminding the March 20, 1995, gas attack, which killed 12 people and made 6,000 ill.
